subject: Agriculture
title: Insects That Eat Crops
description: A 60-second lesson on Insects That Eat Crops.

hook.text: Insects destroy 20% of global crop production every year—enough to feed a billion people.

buildup.text: Chewing insects eat leaves and stems. Sucking insects drain sap. Boring insects tunnel into stalks and fruit.

discovery.text: A single locust can eat its body weight in food daily. A swarm of billions can strip a region bare in hours.

twist.text: Only about 1% of insect species are crop pests. The other 99% are beneficial or neutral.

climax.text: Killing all insects would collapse agriculture—pollination, decomposition, and pest control all depend on them.

punchline.text: 1% of insects cause the damage. We need the other 99% to survive.

quiz.question: What percentage of insect species are actual crop pests?

details.summary: Crop-eating insects destroy an estimated 20-40% of global agricultural production annually. This topic covers the major insect pest groups—beetles, caterpillars, aphids, and locusts—their feeding strategies, and the economic damage they inflict on food systems.
details.whyItMatters: Insect pests cause hundreds of billions of dollars in crop losses each year. Understanding their biology and feeding behavior is the foundation for developing effective, sustainable pest management strategies.
takeaways: Insects destroy 20-40% of global crop production worth hundreds of billions annually
Major pest groups include beetles, caterpillars, aphids, whiteflies, and locusts
Chewing insects consume leaves and stems while sucking insects drain plant sap

faq.question: Which insects cause the most crop damage worldwide?
faq.answer: Aphids, stem borers, bollworms, whiteflies, and locusts are among the most destructive globally. The fall armyworm alone threatens maize across Africa and Asia. Rice stem borers devastate Asian rice crops, and the Colorado potato beetle damages potato production worldwide.

faq.question: How do crop-eating insects damage plants?
faq.answer: Chewing insects like caterpillars and beetles consume leaves, stems, and roots directly. Sucking insects like aphids and whiteflies drain plant sap, weakening plants and often transmitting viral diseases. Some insects also bore into fruits, stems, and grain stores.
